producer_report.summary: pr_commits now classifies each commit in remote_base..head from its content, with no trailers. It reuses the gate's closing_jobs. Rules, per commit and against its first parent's rules: (1) closing_jobs non-empty gives job_landing with that job and its verification id, and verification.json must be in the tree; (2) an added records/interventions/<month>/<id>.json gives declared_intervention; (3) a changed fingerprint is an error naming the sha; (4) otherwise records_only. closing_jobs is now pub, and a new gate helper, added_interventions, lists intervention records a commit adds. PrCommit carries kind, job and verification. GitLandingRecords::commits maps and validates them. The intent errors clearly when no commit lands a job. Fixtures in the core reconcile tests, the gh records_flow tests and the CLI reconcile test now build real job-landing commits; the CLI uses one shared pr_head helper. The old trailer-test in gh.rs is replaced. Docs §5.3 and the failure table, and the CHANGELOG, describe content-based classification. The CHANGELOG entry lists every caller and writer with its covering test or the reason it needed no change, and the commands run. The commit message body must carry the same text; Athena writes the commit, so the body is not in the diff. Full `cargo test --locked` exited 0 (background run); clippy and fmt are clean.

criteria_check.criterion: Run `cargo test -p athena-core land::`. A realistic-range test (reading, dispatch and introspection commits, an owner-path commit under a directory with a nested .gitattributes '* athena-exclude', an intervention adding records/interventions/<month>/<id>.json, then a job's candidate, verification and outcome; no Athena-Job trailers) yields records_only x4, declared_intervention, and job_landing carrying that job and its verification id.

It asserts the six shas in order, kinds [RecordsOnly x4, DeclaredIntervention, JobLanding], and the last commit's job and verification id. criteria_check.criterion: Run `cargo test -p athena-core land::`. Blocked-then-landed: a commit adding candidate, verification and a blocked outcome is records_only; a later commit adding only outcome-landed.json plus governed work is job_landing for that job, reusing the gate's closing_jobs.

open_issues: Commit message body: I cannot write it; Athena commits. The CHANGELOG entry holds the full description (callers, writers, covering tests, commands) and can be copied into the body.
run.rs and drain.rs are listed as deliverables but left unchanged, as the plan said: neither calls pr_commits. The description says so.

LandingIntent::validate (athena-data, not a deliverable) requires at least one job id, so a pull request with only intervention or records-only commits gets a clear error and no intent. Should that be relaxed in a later job?
The `cargo test -p athena-cli` run I started last printed only part of its output; its full result is not in my report. The earlier full `cargo test --locked` passed.
mistakes: First fixture for core reconcile tests reused one job id for every pull request, so a later pull request's records were modifications and not closing records; the reconcile tests failed until each pull request got its own job id.
learnings: JobFiles::load silently skips records that do not parse and AnyRecord::parse requires totals on a request job's outcome, so fixtures must build records from athena_data types.
closing_jobs counts only status 'A' paths, so two pull requests in one repository that add the same job's records need distinct jobs; the second would be a modification.
records/ is excluded from the fingerprint by athena-git's attrs, so a records-only fixture needs no .gitattributes.
pr_commits is called only from gh.rs GitLandingRecords::commits; run.rs retry_landing and drain.rs PrLander reach it only through gh::land_pr.
